items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Joe Wilder, my dear friend whom I hired dozens of times to play in my classical and jazz groups.

ctx.x: Did you have to beat the bushes to find musicians that wanted to play this stuff with you?

No, that I didn’t, again, because of New York. Already then you could find – I had in those early groups, four or five of the players were my colleagues in the Metropolitan Opera. Then I had guys who were in the jazz field. Joe Wilder. He was a completely classically trained musician. He could play anything. That’s why he is on the recording that we made of my totally classical, non-jazz brass symphony, Symphony for Brass and Percussion. There’s Bernie Glow and Joe Wilder sitting in the trumpet section. I swear…

items.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I played with the Smithsonian Jazz Masterworks Orchestra, and that’s under the direction of Gunther Schuller

ctx.x: In the past few years you’ve played with the Smithsonian —
Yeah I played with the Smithsonian Jazz Masterworks Orchestra, and that’s under the direction of Gunther Schuller and Dave Baker.
Yeah? How often is that group together?

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Gunther Schuller put the orchestra together. He didn’t go on the tour. Mel Lewis was sort of the leader of the band.
